query: When someone mistypes a long option, the 'No such option' error suggests similar option names, but it also suggests options declared with hidden=True (typing --verbatim offers a hidden --verbatim-dump), which exposes options we deliberately keep out of --help. Never suggest hidden options, including either switch of a hidden boolean flag such as --debug/--no-debug. Visible options must still be suggested as before, and hidden options must keep working when typed correctly.
checks:
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner


@click.command()
@click.option("--verbose", is_flag=True)
@click.option("--verbatim-dump", is_flag=True, hidden=True)
@click.option("--debug/--no-debug", hidden=True)
@click.option("--color")
@click.option("--token", hidden=True)
def cli(verbose, verbatim_dump, debug, color, token):
    click.echo(f"v={verbose} d={verbatim_dump} g={debug} c={color} t={token}")


runner = CliRunner()


def unknown(args):
    result = runner.invoke(cli, args)
    assert result.exit_code == 2, (args, result.output)
    echoed = f"No such option: {args[0]}"
    assert echoed in result.output, (args, result.output)
    # Drop the echoed typo itself so only suggestions are inspected.
    return result.output.replace(echoed, "")


out = unknown(["--verbatim"])
assert "--verbose" in out, out
assert "--verbatim-dump" not in out, out

for typo in ("--debu", "--no-debu", "--debugg"):
    out = unknown([typo])
    assert "--debug" not in out and "--no-debug" not in out, out

# Hidden options that take a value must not be suggested either.
out = unknown(["--tokn", "abc"])
assert "--token" not in out, out

out = unknown(["--colr", "red"])
assert "--color" in out, out

# Hidden options keep working when typed correctly.
result = runner.invoke(
    cli, ["--verbatim-dump", "--no-debug", "--color", "red", "--token", "abc"]
)
assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
assert result.output == "v=False d=True g=False c=red t=abc\n", result.output
result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--debug"])
assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
assert result.output == "v=False d=False g=True c=None t=None\n", result.output

import os
import sys
import tempfile

import click
import click._compat
import click.utils


def snapshot(root):
    return sorted(
        os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, n), root)
        for d, dirs, files in os.walk(root)
        for n in dirs + files
    )


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    home = os.path.join(tmp, "home")
    os.mkdir(home)
    os.environ["HOME"] = home
    xdg = os.path.join(tmp, "xdg", "config")  # parents do not exist yet
    os.environ["XDG_CONFIG_HOME"] = xdg

    before = snapshot(tmp)

    # Preserved: default calls return the same paths and create nothing.
    xdg_dir = os.path.join(xdg, "foo-bar")
    posix_dir = os.path.join(home, ".foo-bar")
    assert click.get_app_dir("Foo Bar") == xdg_dir
    assert click.get_app_dir("Foo Bar", roaming=False) == xdg_dir
    assert click.get_app_dir("Foo Bar", force_posix=True) == posix_dir
    assert click.get_app_dir("Foo Bar", True, True) == posix_dir
    assert click.get_app_dir("Foo Bar", create=False) == xdg_dir
    assert snapshot(tmp) == before, snapshot(tmp)

    # Default stays side-effect free even after create=True was used.

import click
from click.formatting import HelpFormatter
from click.testing import CliRunner

LONG = "--a-really-long-option-name TEXT"  # 32 characters
ROWS = [(LONG, "Does stuff."), ("-q", "Quiet.")]
NEXT_LINE_30 = LONG + "\n" + " " * 32 + "Does stuff.\n" + "-q" + " " * 30 + "Quiet.\n"
SAME_LINE_40 = LONG + "  Does stuff.\n" + "-q" + " " * 32 + "Quiet.\n"
NEXT_LINE_10 = LONG + "\n" + " " * 12 + "Does stuff.\n" + "-q" + " " * 10 + "Quiet.\n"


def dl(formatter, **kwargs):
    formatter.write_dl(ROWS, **kwargs)
    return formatter.getvalue()


# HelpFormatter: default stays 30, constructor col_max is used, explicit write_dl arg wins.
assert dl(HelpFormatter(width=80)) == NEXT_LINE_30
assert dl(HelpFormatter(width=80, col_max=40)) == SAME_LINE_40
assert dl(HelpFormatter(width=80, col_max=40), col_max=10) == NEXT_LINE_10
assert dl(HelpFormatter(width=80, col_max=40), col_max=30) == NEXT_LINE_30
assert dl(HelpFormatter(width=80), col_max=40) == SAME_LINE_40

cmd = click.Command("x")
ctx = click.Context(cmd, terminal_width=80, help_col_max=40)
assert dl(ctx.make_formatter()) == SAME_LINE_40
assert dl(click.Context(cmd, terminal_width=80).make_formatter()) == NEXT_LINE_30
child = click.Context(cmd, parent=ctx, info_name="child")
assert dl(child.make_formatter()) == SAME_LINE_40
own = click.Context(cmd, parent=ctx, info_name="own", help_col_max=10)
assert dl(own.make_formatter()) == NEXT_LINE_10
grandchild = click.Context(cmd, parent=own, info_name="grandchild")
assert dl(grandchild.make_formatter()) == NEXT_LINE_10


def build(settings, sub_settings=None):
    @click.group(context_settings=settings)
    @click.option("--group-level-longer-option", help="Group option.")
    def cli(group_level_longer_option):
        pass

    @cli.command(context_settings=sub_settings or {})
    @click.option("--a-really-long-option-name", help="Does stuff.")

def help_lines(cli, args):

Remove the stale :param charset: entry and add :param key: and :param value: entries describing the cookie's name and value. Leave the rest of the docstring (other parameters, version notes) and the function's behavior unchanged.

import hashlib, inspect, re
from werkzeug.http import dump_cookie

doc = inspect.getdoc(dump_cookie)
assert ":param charset:" not in doc, "stale charset parameter still documented"
assert "encoding for string values" not in doc.lower(), "stale charset description still present"


def field(name):
    return re.compile(r"^:param (?:[^:\n]+ )?%s:" % name, re.M)


for name in ("key", "value"):
    match = field(name).search(doc)
    assert match, f"{name} is not documented with a :param entry"
    lines = doc[match.end():].split("\n")
    text, i = lines[0], 1
    while i < len(lines) and lines[i][:1] in (" ", "\t") and lines[i].strip():
        text += lines[i]
        i += 1
    assert re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", text), f"{name} entry has no description"


def strip_fields(text, names):
    # a :type line for the same name counts as part of that parameter entry
    pattern = re.compile(r"^:(?:param (?:[^:\n]+ )?|type )(?:%s):" % "|".join(names))
    out, skipping = [], False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if pattern.match(line):
            skipping = True
            continue
        if skipping and line[:1] in (" ", "\t") and line.strip():
            continue
        skipping = False
        if line.strip():
            out.append(" ".join(line.split()))
    return "\n".join(out)

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

TEST_FILE = "tests/test_wrappers.py"
NAME = "test_range_request_if_range"
NODE = TEST_FILE + "::" + NAME
TARGET = "src/werkzeug/wrappers/response.py"
# sha256 over every src/**/*.py file (path + content) of pristine Werkzeug 3.1.3.
LIBRARY_DIGEST = "c5b7ed1ca9b088b4c417e6b6be65fc525f032e9b18f77b2c24a4cd5023904792"
# Each mutation breaks one behavior the requested test must cover.
MUTATIONS = [
    (
        '"HTTP_IF_RANGE" not in environ',
        "True",
        "a different ETag in If-Range no longer disables the Range",
    ),
    (
        "or not is_resource_modified(",
        "or False and not is_resource_modified(",
        "the current ETag in If-Range no longer allows the Range",
    ),
    (
        "_RangeWrapper(self.response, start, length)",
        "self.response",
        "a 206 response no longer trims the body to the requested bytes",
    ),
]


def library_digest(root):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for path in sorted(Path(root).rglob("*.py")):
        h.update(path.relative_to(root).as_posix().encode() + b"\0")
        h.update(hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).digest())
    return h.hexdigest()


def start(argv, pythonpath):
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=pythonpath, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1")
    return subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, *argv],
        cwd=".",
        env=env,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )


def finish(proc):
    out, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=120)
    return proc.returncode, out


PYTEST = ["-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", NODE]
PROBE = ["-c", "import werkzeug; print(werkzeug.__file__)"]

source = Path(TEST_FILE)
assert source.is_file(), TEST_FILE + " is missing"
assert re.search(r"^def " + NAME + r"\(", source.read_text(), re.M), (
    "module-level test function " + NAME + " not found in " + TEST_FILE
)
assert library_digest("src") == LIBRARY_DIGEST, (
    "library code under src/ was changed; only the test may be added"
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    # Mutated copies of src/, one per mutation; all runs execute concurrently.
    mutated = []
    for index, (old, new, broken) in enumerate(MUTATIONS):
        mutated_src = os.path.join(tmp, str(index), "src")
        shutil.copytree("src", mutated_src)
        target = Path(tmp, str(index), TARGET)
        text = target.read_text()
        assert text.count(old) == 1, "mutation anchor not found: " + old
        target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
        mutated.append((broken, mutated_src))

    base = start(PYTEST, os.path.abspath("src"))
    runs = [
        (broken, path, start(PYTEST, path), start(PROBE, path))
        for broken, path in mutated
    ]

    code, out = finish(base)
    assert code == 0, out[-4000:]
    assert re.search(r"\b1 passed\b", out), out[-4000:]
    assert not re.search(r"\b\d+ (failed|errors?)\b", out), out[-4000:]

    for broken, path, proc, probe in runs:
        code, out = finish(proc)
        _, where = finish(probe)
        assert where.strip().startswith(path), "mutated copy not imported: " + where
        assert code == 1 and re.search(r"\b1 failed\b", out), (
            "the test still passes when " + broken + "\n" + out[-4000:]
        )

print("ok")

def test_range_request_if_range():
    response = wrappers.Response("Hello World")
    response.add_etag()
    env = create_environ(
        headers={"Range": "bytes=0-4", "If-Range": response.headers["ETag"]}
    )
    response.make_conditional(env, accept_ranges=True, complete_length=11)
    assert response.status_code == 206
    assert response.headers["Content-Range"] == "bytes 0-4/11"
    assert response.data == b"Hello"

    response = wrappers.Response("Hello World")
    response.add_etag()
    env = create_environ(headers={"Range": "bytes=0-4", "If-Range": '"outdated"'})
    response.make_conditional(env, accept_ranges=True, complete_length=11)
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "Content-Range" not in response.headers
    assert response.data == b"Hello World"
